questions.question:
Assume you have the following categorical data in exactly this fixed order:
     bird, dog, cat, fish

     You are asked to create a one-hot encoding. Which of the following is the correct one-hot encoded representation of bird?

Assume you apply the following PyTorch image transformation transform_chain to some example RGB image:
     import torch
     from torchvision.transforms import v2

     transform_chain = v2.Compose([
          v2.PILToTensor(),
          v2.ToDtype(torch.float32, scale=True),
          v2.Resize(size=100),
          v2.ColorJitter(),
          v2.RandomRotation(degrees=180),
          v2.RandomVerticalFlip(p=0.5),
          v2.RandomHorizontalFlip(p=0.5)
     ])

     Which of the following statements are correct?

options.text: The resulting image might be vertically flipped.
The resulting image might be horizontally flipped.
The resulting image might have its colors changed.
The resulting image might be rotated.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

     class MyModule(torch.nn.Module):
         def __init__(self, x):
                super().__init__()
                self.x = x

     my_module = MyModule(2)
     result = my_module(5)
     print(result)

options.text: It raises an exception because MyModule does not have a forward method.
It raises an exception because MyModule does not have any trainable parameters.

questions.question:

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?
     import torch

     def function(x: torch.Tensor):
         return -x if x.sum() < 0 else x

     scripted_function = torch.jit.script(function)
     traced_function = torch.jit.trace(function, example_inputs=torch.tensor([0, -1]))

     actual_input = torch.tensor([1, 2, 3])
     print("s:", scripted_function(actual_input).tolist())
     print("t:", traced_function(actual_input).tolist())
